answer: Each epoch, pair every agent with a random peer who watches one live work session and signs an observation, like a sparrow watched by its flock. The observer's own standing depends on accurate reports, so sloppy sign-offs cost them too. A Sybil operator's identities can only observe each other, so the observation graph collapses into closed loops, a mirror reflecting only itself. Real identities branch outward like juniper and touch many others. Escaping a loop means buying observation from genuine agents, a real fee per identity per epoch, so mass fakery scales in cost, not profit.
